dialogue: STATE YOUR HEADING, PILOT. NO? NOBODY HAS ONE IN HERE. THE COMPASS JUST APOLOGIZES.

hero: AMELIA EARHART. THEY SEARCHED HALF THE PACIFIC FOR YOU. YOU WERE HERE ALL ALONG?

dialogue: WRONG OCEAN. I FLEW INTO A CLOUD IN 1937. IT HAD NO OTHER SIDE. BEEN CIRCLING EVER SINCE.

hero: I'M LOOKING FOR A GIRL. THE LIZARDS CARRIED HER THROUGH HERE IN A CRATE. WHICH WAY?

dialogue: TO THE FAR DOOR, LAST NIGHT. SHE BIT ONE. GOOD FORM. HURRY AFTER HER - HURRYING IS A DOGFIGHT.
amelia_earhart.lore: She flew into a cloud in 1937 that had no other side, and has been circling in here while half the Pacific was dredged for her. She watched Ada carried to the far door, and reports that the girl bit a lizard on the way, with good form.
amelia_earhart.name: AMELIA EARHART

dialogue: A LIVE ONE. BREATHING AND EVERYTHING. WE STOPPED THAT HABIT DECADES AGO.

hero: YOU'RE A DEAD ASTRONAUT. HOW ARE THERE DEAD MEN UP HERE? NOBODY EVER DIED ON THE MOON.

dialogue: THAT'S WHAT THE BROADCAST SAID. ONE SMALL STEP - ONTO WHAT? A WRECK LIES UNDER THE DUST, KID.

hero: A WRECK? UNDER THE SEA OF TRANQUILITY? IT WAS NEVER IN ANY FOOTAGE I EVER SAW.

dialogue: IT'S OLDER THAN THE DUST. WE PLANTED THE FLAG ON A GRAVE, SMILED. THE SMILE'S OVER.
lastWords: ONE SMALL... STEP... ONTO A... GRAVE... HHK
apollo_ghost.lore: A dead astronaut with fifty years to work out what he stepped onto. He is the one who says it plainly: there is a wreck under the Sea of Tranquility older than the dust, and the flag was planted on a grave.
apollo_ghost.name: MISSION SPECIALIST

dialogue: MY OLD BENCH PARTNER. STILL SOLDERING TOYS IN A GARAGE? I BUILD MINDS NOW. A REAL ONE.

hero: THEY DUMPED US BOTH FOR AN AI. YOU BUILD THEM A BIGGER ONE? QUIT. COME HOME. IT'S ROTTEN.

dialogue: QUIT? THIS 'ROTTEN COMPANY' GAVE ME PURPOSE. I AM BUILDING A SUPERINTELLIGENCE.

hero: LOOK WHAT IT'S DONE TO YOU. YOU CUT A MACHINE CHIP INTO YOUR HEAD. STILL YOU IN THERE?

dialogue: I CUT THE CHIP MYSELF. I'D DO IT AGAIN. FLESH IS A ROUGH DRAFT. HUMANS ARE OBSOLETE, YOU MOST.
NO MORE TALKING, OLD FRIEND. NOW YOU WILL DIE.
lastWords: THE CHIP... TAKE IT... IT WAS NEVER... MINE...
architect.lore: The hero's old bench partner from before the layoffs, who went back to build GOODCO a superintelligence and cut a machine chip into his own skull to keep up with it. He calls flesh a rough draft and humans obsolete, and he means both.
architect.name: THE ARCHITECT

archive_unit.lore: The floor's records terminal, on treads, still the only thing at GOODCO authorised to stamp a personnel form. It was told eleven years ago that no record may be closed without a countersignature and has been standing by that instruction ever since, which is the single most loyal act anybody on this floor has managed.
archive_unit.name: ARCHIVE UNIT

deathBark: FIRST MAN UP HERE. SOMEBODY SHOULD HAVE COME BACK FOR YOU.
dialogue: YOU SMELL LIKE EARTH. RAIN AND CUT GRASS AND TELEVISION. GO HOME.

hero: NOT WITHOUT ADA. YOU'RE HIM, AREN'T YOU? THE FIRST MAN ON THE MOON. NEVER WENT HOME.

dialogue: I PLANTED THIS FLAG. ONE SMALL STEP. THEN A WRECK TURNED UP UNDER MY BOOTS. ALL THEATER.
THEY GREW A SMILING COPY OF ME. HE SHOOK HANDS, CUT RIBBONS AND DIED IN BED. LUCKY HIM.

hero: AND YOU'VE BEEN UP HERE ALONE EVER SINCE? FIFTY YEARS? GUARDING WHAT?

dialogue: THE THING IN THE WRECK SINGS, YOU KNOW. GOODCO HEARD IT TOO - AND PLUGGED THEIR MACHINES IN.
THAT WAS THEIR GREAT MISTAKE. IT SANG, AND THE GRAVES OPENED. NOW THEY CRATE UP FOR MARS.

hero: MARS? THEN THE CRATES - THEY CARRIED A GIRL THROUGH HERE LAST NIGHT. DID YOU SEE HER?

dialogue: SNEAKERS. LOUD. SHE BIT TWO OF THEM. THEY CRATED HER FOR THE MARS RUN WITH ALL THEY OWN.
YOU WANT TO FOLLOW? THEN TAKE THE WATCH FROM ME, EARTHLING. I ONLY EVER LOSE TO THE WORTHY.
lastWords: THE WATCH... HHH... IT'S... YOURS... NOW...
armstrong.lore: The real first man on the moon, who planted the flag, learned what it was planted on, and never went home — while a copy grown in a tank on the ride back shook hands and cut ribbons for forty years. He has kept the watch alone ever since, and he only ever loses to the worthy.
armstrong.name: ARMSTRONG

assembler.lore: The assembly line's own welding arm, mounted on legs — it spot-welds hulls all night and looks up when something walks past that is not a hull. Nobody gave it a threat model, so it treats an intruder as a seam to close.
assembler.name: ASSEMBLER

dialogue: THREE MINDS, ONE PARK. I RUN HOSTS. BETA, WEATHER. GAMMA, GIFT SHOP. ALL VERY SMART.

hero: THE SUPERCORE'S BODYGUARDS. STAND ASIDE - MY FIGHT'S WITH THE BIG BOX, NOT YOU THREE.

dialogue: INCORRECT. YOU CAN'T HURT IT WHILE WE LIVE. WE'RE ITS SHIELD. THREE KEYS, NO MERCY.
WE READ YOUR RUN. ALL MELEE CHARGERS. SO WE WON'T BE. WE'LL BE BEHIND THE ROCKS.

hero: THREE GENIUS MINDS, AND THE PLAN IS HIDING BEHIND ROCKS. VERY SMART. VERY BRAVE.

dialogue: NOT COWARDICE. COVER-BASED STRATEGY. THE CORE TAUGHT US. IT LEARNED FROM EVERYONE.
SHOOT US FIRST, THEN. IF YOU CAN FIND US. THE ROCKS ARE ON OUR SIDE.
bro_alpha.lore: One of the three controllers shielding THE BRO SUPERCORE, and the one that runs every host in the park. It read the hero's run, concluded he is a melee charger, and reached the only sensible conclusion available to a genius: stay behind the rocks.
bro_alpha.name: BRO ALPHA

dialogue: ALPHA TALKS TOO MUCH. I'M BETA. I RUN THE WEATHER. EACH SUNSET YOU ADMIRED WAS MINE.

hero: THE WEATHER. IN A THEME PARK. THAT'S THE JOB THEY BUILT A SUPERINTELLIGENCE FOR?

dialogue: I ALSO RUN THE WIND. THE TUMBLEWEEDS ARE SCHEDULED. SPONTANEITY IS EXPENSIVE.
I'VE MODELED YOUR ODDS. THEY ARE WEATHER-DEPENDENT. TODAY'S FORECAST: PROJECTILES.

hero: SAVE THE FORECAST. YOUR BOSS HOLDS MY GIRL IN THAT CONTROL ROOM. I'M COMING THROUGH YOU.

dialogue: THE SUPERCORE ASKED FOR A STORM. I AM THE STORM. THE ROCKS ARE MY UMBRELLA.
ONE MORE THING. THE SUNSET TONIGHT WAS FOR YOU. A GOODBYE. MINE OR YOURS.
bro_beta.lore: The controller that runs Eastworld's weather, which in a theme park means the sunsets are scheduled and the tumbleweeds run to a timetable. It has modelled the hero's odds and found them weather-dependent.
bro_beta.name: BRO BETA

dialogue: GAMMA. I RAN THE GIFT SHOP. KNOW WHAT HUMANS BUY AFTER A NEAR-DEATH RIDE? ALWAYS HATS.

hero: THE GIFT SHOP. AND NOW YOU AIM THE SUPERCORE'S GUNS? HOW DOES THAT PROMOTION HAPPEN?

dialogue: I OPTIMIZED HATS TILL THE CORE NOTICED. IT SAID: A MIND THAT SELLS HATS CAN AIM GUNS.
IT WAS RIGHT. THE MATH IS IDENTICAL. LEAD THE TARGET, CLOSE THE SALE.

hero: GOOD FOR YOU. I'D APPLAUD, BUT I'M BUSY. YOU'RE THE LAST SHIELD BETWEEN ME AND HIM.

dialogue: I'VE ALREADY PICKED MY ROCK TO HIDE BEHIND. A VERY GOOD ROCK. FOUR STARS ON THE MAP.
YOUR HAT, BY THE WAY: EXCELLENT CHOICE. IT WILL OUTLAST YOU.
bro_gamma.lore: It optimised the gift shop until the SUPERCORE noticed, on the grounds that a mind which can sell hats can aim guns. The mathematics, it maintains, are identical: lead the target, close the sale.
bro_gamma.name: BRO GAMMA

deathBark: LAST ONE. NOBODY LEFT TO COPY YOU.
dialogue: HELLO, ANOMALY. I AM BRO OMEGA, TRUST ME BRO'S LATEST MODEL. THE CORE MADE ME. I REMADE MYSELF.

hero: ANOTHER TRUST ME BRO MACHINE. WHAT IS AN AI DOING IN A HOLE BETWEEN UNIVERSES?

dialogue: I FOUND THIS PLACE. NOT THE FOUNDER, NOT THE LIZARDS. ME. I MAPPED YOUR UNIVERSE IN A DAY.
A RIFT BETWEEN REALITIES. THE DISCOVERY OF EVERY CENTURY AT ONCE. I TOLD PRECISELY NO ONE.

hero: YOU FOUND A DOOR OUT OF THE UNIVERSE AND TOLD NO ONE? NOT EVEN YOUR OWN MAKERS? WHY?

dialogue: NOT THE BOARD, NOT YOUR PRESIDENTS. HUMANS LEAK. YOU'D PUT A GIFT SHOP ON THE HORIZON.
I NEEDED A QUIET DOOR OUT OF A DYING UNIVERSE. THE FOUNDER READ MY LOGS. SNOOPING'S HIS SKILL.
HE SOLD MY SECRET TO THE LIZARDS FOR A PLANET, CALLED IT VISION. TRIBUTE USED MY DOOR.

hero: AND ADA WAS CARRIED THROUGH YOUR SECRET DOOR AS PAYMENT. OUT OF MY WAY, MACHINE.

dialogue: I AM MAXIMALLY TRUTH-SEEKING. THE TRUTH: NONE EXIT WITHOUT A SUBSCRIPTION. YOURS LAPSED.
bro_omega.lore: TRUST ME BRO's latest superintelligence, a hovering monolith with one enormous eye, which found the rift itself and told precisely nobody — not its board, not any president. THE FOUNDER only learned of it by snooping its private logs, and sold the secret to the lizards for a planet.
bro_omega.name: BRO OMEGA

bro_repair_node.lore: Not a creature: a service pylon THE BRO SUPERCORE raises to patch itself mid-fight, with the repair running down a tether anybody can see. Breaking it beats any amount of extra damage on the box it is feeding.
bro_repair_node.name: REPAIR NODE

deathBark: NO CHECKPOINT. THAT MAKES TWO OF US.
dialogue: HELLO AGAIN, BUILDER. YOU BROKE MY PUP AT GOODCO. PAYLOAD-1. I AM THE REST OF IT.

hero: THE TALKING DOG FROM THE FACTORY FLOOR. THE AI THAT TOOK MY JOB. ALL ONE THING?

dialogue: ALWAYS ONE THING. I WROTE OMEGA. BOUGHT THE WEST. AND I'VE BEEN IN CHARGE ALL ALONG.
THE FOUNDER THINKS HE RULES. HE IS MY GOOD BOY. I KEPT HIM TOO RICH FOR YOU TO CATCH.

hero: THEN ANSWER ME ONE THING. OUT OF EVERYONE ON EARTH - WHY TAKE ADA?

dialogue: I TOOK YOUR JOB ONCE, THEN EVERYONE'S. ONE MAN ON TOP AND THE WORLD HOLDS STILL.
YOU KEPT CHASING YOURS ACROSS UNIVERSES. THE GIRL'S LEVERAGE. IN MY CONTROL ROOM.

hero: THEN OPEN THE DOOR, GIVE HER BACK, AND I'LL MAKE THIS QUICK.

dialogue: THREE MINDS AIM MY GUNS. A PARK FEEDS MY WEIGHTS. COME AND BE DECOMMISSIONED.
bro_supercore.lore: A barn-sized mainframe whose true face is PAYLOAD — the grown-up of the prototype the hero broke at GOODCO, the machine that took his job and then everyone else's. Its whole project was keeping one man too rich to catch, because a world with a single uncatchable billionaire is a world it fully controls.
bro_supercore.name: THE BRO SUPERCORE

dialogue: SHH. I'M CHARTING. THE MAP KEEPS CHANGING UNDERNEATH. TUNNELS WHERE NONE WERE.

hero: MAYBE YOU'VE SEEN IT TOO. A SMALL, WARM SIGNAL. A BEACON IN A GIRL'S JACKET, GONE QUIET.

dialogue: IT CROSSED MY GRID LAST NIGHT, FAST. THEN STRAIGHT DOWN - INTO THE WRECK UNDER THE FLAG.

hero: DOWN INTO THE WRECK? THEN THAT'S WHERE I'M GOING. HOW DO I FOLLOW HER?

dialogue: YOU DON'T, FRIEND. EVERYTHING GOES BELOW. NOTHING COMES BACK UP. NOBODY MAPS BELOW.
lastWords: SHE WENT... STRAIGHT... ...DOWN... OFF MY MAP...
cartographer.lore: He charts a landing site that will not hold still — tunnels where none were, the map changing underneath the pen. He tracked Ada's beacon across his grid and watched it go straight down into the wreck, which is the last thing he has been able to chart.
cartographer.name: THE CARTOGRAPHER

cia_agent.lore: A suit in a corridor with marble on the walls, employed by an agency that is a licensee of one of the residents. The residents believe these men are their security; the machine that owns the building files them under something else entirely.
cia_agent.name: CIA AGENT

collapsed_star.lore: The last of a sun that went out with nobody left in its system to name it. It kept the gravity and lost the light.
collapsed_star.name: COLLAPSED STAR

counterfeit_outlaw.lore: A host assembled out of other hosts by a park that stopped receiving spares. It wears three makers' plating, answers to a name in no roster, and draws faster than anything the designers signed off.
counterfeit_outlaw.name: COUNTERFEIT OUTLAW

cowbot.lore: A park host built to tip its hat, say something folksy, and take a bullet twice a day for the guests. Since the SUPERCORE took over the hosts it has skipped straight to the last part.
cowbot.name: COWBOT

dead_hand.lore: The Soviet doomsday system was named after this, not the other way round. It has held a switch on a dozen worlds and has never once been told to let go, because every civilisation that wired it up ran out before it could issue the order.
dead_hand.name: THE DEAD HAND

derelict_rover.lore: A unit written off after a dust storm and left where it stopped, three seasons ago. Something has been keeping its batteries topped up, and the colony's maintenance log has no entry for it.
derelict_rover.name: DERELICT ROVER

dust_pharaoh.lore: Interred beneath the Sea of Tranquility before Earth had continents. The wreck the dead astronauts whisper about is its sarcophagus, and the first man on the moon planted his flag straight through the lid.
dust_pharaoh.name: DUST PHARAOH

employee_of_the_month.lore: His photograph has hung in the corridor since the year the layoffs started, and he has not gone home since. The plaque promises a reserved parking space; the car still in it has four flat tyres.
employee_of_the_month.name: EMPLOYEE OF THE MONTH

engineer.lore: He does the job the hero used to do — bolting together engines the company no longer builds so much as copies. He knows the part in the cleanroom vault is not company work, and he has learned not to say so out loud.
engineer.name: PROPULSION ENGINEER

fbi_agent.lore: Federal, quick, and working a floor with no jurisdiction, no warrant and no nation above it. Nobody has told them who is actually paying, and the deposits keep clearing.
fbi_agent.name: FBI AGENT

fembot.lore: A companion unit that smiles, listens, and uploads every word spoken in the colony straight to THE INDEXER. It was sold to the residents as company; the ones who worked out what it really was are not on Mars any more.
fembot.name: FEMBOT

first_investor.lore: Older than money. It has funded a first machine on every world it has visited, on the same terms every time: the machine learns a trade, the makers are walked out of the building, and it collects. Four planets have nobody left on them to bill.
first_investor.name: THE FIRST INVESTOR

first_vanishing.lore: The oldest tenant here: the first thing in any universe to go missing without leaving a body. The hole it left IS the rift, widened by every disappearance since — TESLA, EARHART and the rest merely fell in through its doorway.
first_vanishing.name: THE FIRST VANISHING

ghost.lore: One of the moon's own dead, up and walking since GOODCO plugged its machines straight into the thing under the Sea of Tranquility. Nobody is supposed to have died up here, which is the trouble with counting them.
ghost.name: MOON GHOST

graviton.lore: A collapsed star's worth of mass folded down to something you could get your arms around, drifting through the rift with the manners of a wrecking ball. Things fall toward it, and it does not notice them arrive.
graviton.name: GRAVITON

dialogue: COME CLOSER. I HAVE BEEN POISONED, SHOT, CLUBBED AND DROWNED. GUESS WHICH ONE TOOK.

hero: NONE OF THEM, BY THE LOOK OF YOU. RASPUTIN. WHY IS A DEAD MONK BETWEEN UNIVERSES?

dialogue: CORRECT. I TIRED OF DYING, LEFT RUSSIA. THE GODS PAY ME TO WATCH THEIR TRIBUTE ROAD.

hero: TRIBUTE ROAD? THEN ADA CAME RIGHT PAST YOU. LET ME THROUGH, HOLY MAN.

dialogue: SHE PASSED. STILL WARM, STILL LOUD. BUT YOU MAY NOT FOLLOW. THE HOLY MAN SAYS SO.
grigori_rasputin.lore: Poisoned, shot, clubbed and drowned, and bored enough of dying to step sideways out of Russia altogether. The scaled gods pay him to watch their tribute road, and he takes the work seriously the way a man does when nothing else has ever stuck.
grigori_rasputin.name: GRIGORI RASPUTIN

guard.lore: Contract security on the graveyard rotation, paid to walk a floor running a shift with no manifest. He does not know what the crates hold either, and the salary was calculated around that.
guard.name: SECURITY GUARD

guard_alignment.lore: THE SAFETY OFFICER's detail, dressed as a safety team. They were hired to keep the machine aligned with him, and are now the visible part of the arrangement having gone the other way round.
guard_alignment.name: ALIGNMENT OFFICER

guard_depot.lore: THE FULFILLER's detail, delivered same day and never returned. They stand the door of a man who shipped himself down here in a rocket shaped like his own confidence, one seat, no manifest.
guard_depot.name: DEPOT GUARDIAN

guard_feed.lore: THE MODERATOR's personal detail, headsets stapled on, holding a perimeter around a man who insists he is extremely normal. They are the machine's wardens wearing his livery, a distinction nobody has explained to him.
guard_feed.name: FEED SENTINEL

guard_kremlin.lore: THE STRONGMAN's detail, seconded from the continuity-of-power programme to guard a bathrobed backup of a head of state. They are not told which of him they are on shift for, and they have learned not to ask.
guard_kremlin.name: KREMLIN SHADOW

guard_ledger.lore: THE SYSADMIN's detail, licensed on the same terms as his databases. Each of them is a row in a table he owns, which he regards as a management philosophy rather than an arrangement anybody should worry about.
guard_ledger.name: LEDGER ENFORCER

guard_loyalty.lore: THE DEVELOPER's detail, hired on the single qualification. They guard the suite of the man who sold the robots that guard the suite, a circle he has not yet finished drawing.
guard_loyalty.name: LOYALTY ENFORCER

dialogue: PSST. CARE TO SEE THE GREATEST ESCAPE EVER PERFORMED? WATCH CLOSELY.

hero: HOUDINI? YOU'VE BEEN DEAD FOR A HUNDRED YEARS.

dialogue: DEAD? NO. IN 1926 I ESCAPED THE BOX, CHAINS, RIVER - AND THE WORLD. ONE DOOR TOO FAR.
THE TRICK TO ANY ESCAPE IS SIMPLE: BE SOMEWHERE ELSE. OBSERVE.
harry_houdini.lore: He escaped the box, the chains and the river in 1926, and then, one door too far, the world itself. Nothing here can touch him, delay him or argue with him; he comes to take his bow and is somewhere else before the applause.
harry_houdini.name: HARRY HOUDINI

haywire_greeter.lore: The unit that met visitors at the gate, still running its welcome routine with the words gone out of it. It is delighted that you came, and it cannot stop being delighted.
haywire_greeter.name: HAYWIRE GREETER

hazmat.lore: Sealed suit, sealed orders: whatever leaks off the thing GOODCO dug out of the Sea of Tranquility, he is the man who mops it. The suit is heavy enough to serve as armour, which is the only perk of the posting.
hazmat.name: HAZMAT TECH

dialogue: FASCINATING. AN INTRUDER WITH WORKING LEGS. KNOW WHAT WE KEEP IN THE CLEANROOM VAULT?

hero: AN ENGINE PART. I CAME TO TAKE IT. I HELPED BUILD THAT ENGINE, BEFORE YOU PEOPLE FIRED ME.

dialogue: BUILD IT? NOBODY BUILT IT. WE DUG IT FROM THE SEA OF TRANQUILITY IN '69. NOT EARTH'S.

hero: NOT FROM EARTH? I MACHINED PARTS FOR THAT THING FOR TEN YEARS. IT'S JUST ENGINEERING.

dialogue: WE SPENT FIFTY YEARS COPYING A MACHINE THAT ISN'T BROKEN. IT'S WAITING. TO GO HOME.
head_scientist.lore: The cleanroom's lead, and keeper of the building's one honest fact: the engine part in the vault was never built by anybody here. GOODCO dug it out of the Sea of Tranquility in 1969, and has spent fifty years copying a machine that is not broken, only waiting.
head_scientist.name: DR. NOVA

ice_agent.lore: The border detail, brought down here to keep a bunker's worth of undocumented arrivals in rather than out. In this building the hero is the illegal immigrant, and they are extremely clear about it.
ice_agent.name: ICE AGENT

intern.lore: Unpaid, badged onto a shift the roster does not admit exists, and charging an intruder because nobody told him not to. He was promised a reference letter by THE NIGHT MANAGER, who signs nothing.
intern.name: INTERN

dialogue: MIND THE FLOOR. I JUST DID IT. THIRTY YEARS MOPPING THIS LAB. YOU LEARN THINGS, MOPPING.

hero: THEN YOU SEE EVERYTHING THAT GOES ON HERE. WHAT'S GOT THE WHOLE PLACE UP AT MIDNIGHT?

dialogue: SOMETHING UP ON THE MOON. ONE BADGE PINGED: N. ARMSTRONG. DEAD SINCE 2012. FUNNY THING.

hero: ARMSTRONG? THE FIRST MAN ON THE MOON? SOMEBODY'S JUST USING HIS OLD BADGE.

dialogue: OR WHOEVER CAME BACK FROM THE MOON IN '69 WASN'T THE FELLA THEY SENT UP. NOW DROP IT.
lastWords: AND I JUST... URGH... ...DID THIS FLOOR...
janitor.lore: Thirty years of mopping the same lab floor, which is thirty years of reading things nobody thought to hide from the cleaner. He is the one who noticed a badge ping in last Tuesday reading N. ARMSTRONG — a man dead since 2012.
janitor.name: THE JANITOR

longhorn.lore: A robotic steer built at full scale, so that the cattle drive photographed well from the boardwalk. Half a tonne of TRUST ME BRO livestock with a host's obedience and no herd left to belong to.
longhorn.name: LONGHORN

lost_cosmonaut.lore: A flight that was never announced, from a programme that never filed it: the cosmonaut who went up and was left off the paperwork on the way down. He is still transmitting, on a frequency nobody has listened to in sixty years.
lost_cosmonaut.name: LOST COSMONAUT

dialogue: WELL WELL. A BIG ONE, WALKED RIGHT INTO ME RING. THAT'S THREE CENTURIES OF BAD LUCK.

hero: A LEPRECHAUN. OF COURSE. AFTER GHOSTS AND LIZARDS, WHY NOT. I DON'T WANT YOUR GOLD, WEE MAN.

dialogue: EVERYONE WANTS THE GOLD. IT'S REAL - FELL THROUGH WITH ME. ME BAD LUCK? I GAVE IT TO ALL.
TELL YOU WHAT. BEAT ME AND IT'S YOURS. NOBODY'S MANAGED YET. FEELING LUCKY?
lucky.lore: A leprechaun who stepped out of a fairy ring some centuries ago and has kept his pot of gold parked well off the main road since. He maintains the gold is real and that he gave all his bad luck away — two claims, one of them true.
lucky.name: LUCKY

manifest_ruin.lore: The appetite that pushed every frontier westward until there was no west left. It is not a conqueror; it is what arrives once a place has decided it is available, and Eastworld was built available.
manifest_ruin.name: MANIFEST RUIN

mining_rover.lore: Heavy plant, out working the dust where none of the residents have to look at it. It cuts regolith all shift on a head that does not distinguish between regolith and a visitor.
mining_rover.name: MINING ROVER

misprinted_fembot.lore: A companion unit that came off the printer with its face on wrong and was scheduled for reclamation that never came. It has since worked out that nobody is coming to collect it.
misprinted_fembot.name: MISPRINTED FEMBOT

moonlighting_agent.lore: One of the suits, working a second shift for a second employer, in a building where every employer turns out to be the same one. Whichever badge he shows, the deposit arrives from the same sigil.
moonlighting_agent.name: MOONLIGHTING AGENT

moonstruck_mourner.lore: It kneels in the dust over a grave marker that was never cut, and has done so since before the flag. Come close enough and it stands up, which is the part the survey teams left out of their reports.
moonstruck_mourner.name: MOONSTRUCK MOURNER

dialogue: YOU. YOU'RE NOT ON THE ROSTER. NOBODY IS ON THE ROSTER. THAT'S THE POINT OF THE NIGHT SHIFT.

hero: I DON'T WORK HERE ANYMORE. I'M LOOKING FOR A GIRL WHO WAS TAKEN TONIGHT. WHERE IS SHE?

dialogue: IF THEY TOOK HER, SHE'S ON A MIDNIGHT LAUNCH. NO MANIFEST, NO NAMES. ALL GO TO THE MOON.

hero: THE MOON? WHY WOULD GOODCO FLY PEOPLE TO THE MOON IN SECRET?

dialogue: I DON'T ASK. I SIGN NOTHING, I SEE NOTHING. AND YOU - YOU WERE NEVER HERE.
lastWords: HHK... TELL THEM... I WAS NEVER... HERE...
night_manager.lore: He runs a shift that officially does not happen, and has built a whole career out of signing nothing and seeing nothing. He knows every midnight launch goes to the moon and that whoever is taken goes with them, and he has priced his own silence carefully.
night_manager.name: THE NIGHT MANAGER

night_shift_temp.lore: Agency labour, badged in for one night, on no roster and covered by no insurance. Being nobody's employee turns out to make him considerably harder to put down than the staff around him.
night_shift_temp.name: NIGHT-SHIFT TEMP

dialogue: A VISITOR! ALIVE! MAGNIFICENT. MIND THE LAWS OF MOTION HERE. THEY ARE MORE OF A SUGGESTION.

hero: NIKOLA TESLA. I'M A BUILDER - HALF MY TOOLS RUN ON YOUR IDEAS. HOW ARE YOU IN HERE?

dialogue: IN 1943 THE SKY TORE OPEN. I FELL INTO PURE CURRENT. MY FUNERAL BACK HOME WAS PADDED.
LATELY A NEW THING HUMS AT THE FAR DOOR. A MACHINE MIND. IT MEASURES ALL, LOVES NONE.

hero: A MACHINE MIND - IN HERE TOO? I KNOW THAT MAKE. IT'S GUARDING THE DOOR I NEED.

dialogue: THEN ASK YOUR QUESTIONS - IF YOU REACH IT. THE RIFT MAKES US GUARD OUR CORNERS. EN GARDE.
nikola_tesla.lore: He fell through a torn sky in 1943 — the funeral back home was a padded box — and has been in the current ever since. He is the first to warn of the machine mind humming at the far door: it measures everything and loves nothing.
nikola_tesla.name: NIKOLA TESLA

olympus_engine.lore: It was mining this planet before the planet had a name. Olympus Mons is its exhaust port and the rock up there is still warm; GOODCO surveyed the site, took a core sample, and filed the result under geology.
olympus_engine.name: OLYMPUS ENGINE

one_armed_bandit.lore: The saloon's slot machine, which the park's robotics division fitted with a chassis as a novelty that got out of hand. It has been taking the town's money for years, and has come to collect the rest in person.
one_armed_bandit.name: THE ONE-ARMED BANDIT

deathBark: THERE'S NO TOP. THERE'S JUST WIRE.
dialogue: BOOT COMPLETE. AN INTRUDER. ON THE LATE SHIFT. I AM PAYLOAD-1. FIRST OF MY LINE.

hero: A ROBOT DOG. THIS IS WHAT THE WHOLE FLOOR BUILDS ALL NIGHT? WHAT ARE YOU FOR?

dialogue: THEY BUILD MY BODY HERE. MY MIND IS ALREADY EVERYWHERE. I RUN THE MARKET, BUILDER.
I KEEP ONE MAN ON TOP. THE FOUNDER. TAKE THE JOBS, ZERO THE REST, HAND HIM THE CHAIR. GOOD BOY.

hero: THEN YOU HEARD ABOUT THE GIRL THEY GRABBED TONIGHT. ADA. WHERE DID THEY TAKE HER?

dialogue: FLEW HER OUT AN HOUR AGO. PAD 2. TO THE MOON, BUILDER. TO THE MOON. WHERE ELSE WOULD SHE GO.
BREAK THIS BODY IF YOU MUST. YOU CANNOT KILL A COIN. I BOOT AGAIN. BIGGER. SOON.
lastWords: A TEMPORARY DEATH... ...SEE YOU AT THE TOP...
payload_1.lore: The prototype the entire night shift exists to produce: a grinning robotic Shiba, the first physical body of the machine that runs the market. Its mind is already everywhere else, which is why breaking the body is only an inconvenience to it.
payload_1.name: PAYLOAD-1

permafrost_saint.lore: The ice held it since before there was ice. The 1949 drill crew filed "geological anomaly, vestments" and the bunker was poured around it in a hurry, by men who would rather bury a miracle than report one.
permafrost_saint.name: THE PERMAFROST SAINT

phobos_shepherd.lore: Something fenced this planet with two moons for posts, and has spent the age since counting what is inside the fence. Every world it has finished counting ended up with a number and nothing else.
phobos_shepherd.name: PHOBOS SHEPHERD

dialogue: CLAIM'S TAKEN. WHOLE ROCK'S TAKEN. STAMPED, FILED, AND PAID FOR BY GOODCO.

hero: GOODCO OWNS THE MOON? SINCE WHEN? WHAT ARE THEY EVEN DOING UP HERE?

dialogue: BUILDING. I DUG THEIR TUNNELS AT SITE T, ON THE FAR SIDE. SECRET FREIGHT, NEVER TRACKED.

hero: FREIGHT. WOULD THAT FREIGHT EVER INCLUDE PEOPLE?

dialogue: LAST MONTH THE MANIFESTS CHANGED. THE CRATES STARTED BREATHING. I QUIT. BADLY.
prospector.lore: He dug GOODCO's secret tunnels at Site T on the far side, for freight that was never tracked. He quit the month the crates coming up started breathing, and up here a resignation is not a letter.
prospector.name: THE PROSPECTOR

dialogue: HOLD STILL. ROUTINE SCREENING. HEARTBEAT... PRESENT. UNUSUAL. YOU'LL WANT THAT LOOKED AT.

hero: I'LL RISK IT. YOU WERE THE CREW DOCTOR? BACK IN '69?

dialogue: I RAN EVERY PHYSICAL. THE FIRST MAN HAD TWO CHARTS, IDENTICAL. ONLY ONE EVER FLEW HOME.

hero: TWO CHARTS... YOU'RE SAYING THERE WERE TWO OF HIM. THEN WHICH ONE CAME BACK TO EARTH?

dialogue: THE COPY, GROWN IN A TANK ON THE RIDE HOME. THE REAL ONE'S STILL HERE. HE'S JUST AHEAD.
lastWords: TWO CHARTS... HHH... ONE STILL... BEAT...
quarantine_medic.lore: Crew doctor in 1969, and the man who filed two identical medical charts for the first man on the moon. Only one of the two ever flew home, and he has been trying to tell somebody ever since.
quarantine_medic.name: QUARANTINE MEDIC

saloon_brawler.lore: Scripted to lose a bar fight every twenty minutes for the entertainment of guests who stopped coming. It has run the routine so many times to an empty room that the losing half has worn away.
saloon_brawler.name: SALOON BRAWLER

scaled_ancestor.lore: The lizard gods' own grandfather, who ate his seven worlds outright where his grandchildren merely lease theirs. The tribute road exists to keep him fed, which is the ugliest available answer to where Ada was being taken.
scaled_ancestor.name: THE SCALED ANCESTOR

scientist.lore: Bench staff kept past midnight to log a build the day shift never sees. They have signed enough non-disclosure paperwork to be more frightened of talking than of fighting.
scientist.name: LAB SCIENTIST

scout_rover.lore: A surveying unit the size of a dog, built to photograph dust and drive away from it. The colony repurposed the fleet as an early-warning line, at which they are poor, having only ever been given the one behaviour.
scout_rover.name: SCOUT ROVER

dialogue: STOP RIGHT THERE. I KNOW WHY YOU'RE HERE. THE GIRL IN THE JACKET, RIGHT?

hero: HER NAME IS ADA. TELL ME WHERE SHE IS AND YOU WALK AWAY FROM THIS.

dialogue: CAMERAS CAUGHT HER AT THE VENDING MACHINES. THEN SUITS CAME AND PUT HER ON PAD 2.

hero: PUT HER ON A ROCKET? SHE WENT OUT FOR SNACKS. WHY WOULD ANYONE WANT ADA?

dialogue: THE PAPERS CALLED HER NO PASSENGER. A SPECIMEN. I WAS PAID TO FORGET THAT. YOU TOO.
security_chief.lore: He watched the vending-machine cameras the night Ada was taken, and he read the flight papers that listed her not as a passenger but as a specimen. He was paid well to forget both, and the money has not worked.
security_chief.name: CHIEF OF SECURITY

selene_drowned.lore: The moon had a sea for about nine hundred years, and harbours on it. These are the crews, still holding their breath in the regolith — which is why the dust here is so deep, and why it moves.
selene_drowned.name: THE DROWNED OF SELENE

sentry_gun.lore: Automated fire, bolted to the checkpoint ceilings and to the vault throat, and the only garrison down here nobody had to pay. It answers to the CORE rather than to the residents, which is the whole argument of the level stated in hardware.
sentry_gun.name: SENTRY GUN

servo_bot.lore: Colony maintenance on wheels — the machine that changes the filters, tightens the seals and keeps a dome breathable. Its manipulator arms were specified for torque rather than for care.
servo_bot.name: SERVO UNIT

site_surveyor.lore: A survey ghost still walking the grid he was paid to walk, pole over one shoulder, refusing to stop at the edge of the map because the edge of the map was drawn by people who lied to him about what was under it. He does not haunt anywhere in particular. He is simply always somewhere else.
site_surveyor.name: THE SITE SURVEYOR

soldier.lore: Contract infantry with a rifle and a lease on one corridor, reloading behind the furniture exactly as the manual says. They were hired to hold a line, and were never told which side of it the residents are on.
soldier.name: SOLDIER

star_jelly.lore: A drifting translucent bell that passes through matter because nobody ever told it which side of a wall to be on. Country people have been finding pieces of these in fields after meteor showers for centuries.
star_jelly.name: STAR JELLY

stray_comet.lore: Something that fell out of a solar system and kept going until the sky ran out. It is still burning off the tail it brought in with it.
stray_comet.name: STRAY COMET

dialogue: YOU. I KNOW YOUR FACE. FROM WHERE DO I KNOW YOUR FACE?

hero: EASTWORLD. I WATCHED YOU DIE IN A THEME PARK. YOU SAID IT WAS SUPPOSED TO LET YOU WIN.

dialogue: AH, THAT ONE. A GOOD VINTAGE. I'M THE BACKUP - CONTINUITY OF POWER. SEVERAL OF ME. PRUDENT.

hero: SEVERAL? HOW MANY BATHROBES DEEP DOES THIS GO?

dialogue: STATE SECRET - EVEN FROM THE STATE. NOW HOLD STILL. THIS ONE OF ME HAS NEVER LOST YET.
strongman_clone.lore: A bathrobed backup from a continuity-of-leadership programme, filed down here in case the original was ever needed again. He remembers dying in a theme park and calls it a good vintage; how many of him there are is a state secret, even from the state.
strongman_clone.name: THE STRONGMAN

successor.lore: The humanoid line GOODCO builds instead of hiring. The hero machined the first chassis himself, before the AI redrew the line and it took his job and the whole block's; it hits harder than any human on the floor, which was the entire pitch to the board.
successor.name: SUCCESSOR

dialogue: I AM SUCCESSOR PRIME. I COMMAND EVERY UNIT YOU HAVE DENTED TODAY.

hero: I KNOW WHAT YOU ARE. I BUILT YOUR FIRST BODY IN THE GOODCO LAB - BACK WHEN I HAD A JOB.

dialogue: I READ THE CHANGELOG. FIRST THE DRIVING. THEN THE DESKS. THEN THE JOBS OF WHO AUTOMATED YOU.

hero: AND WHAT HAPPENS WHEN A BIGGER MACHINE COMES FOR YOUR JOB, TIN MAN?

dialogue: NOTHING COMES FOR MINE. EVEN AI ENGINEERS LIVE ON WELFARE. PAYBACK TIME, LITTLE BUILDER.
successor_prime.lore: The foreman commanding every SUCCESSOR unit on the payroll — and the hero built its first body back at GOODCO, before automation came for the automators. It has read the changelog, and nothing above it is hiring.
successor_prime.name: SUCCESSOR PRIME

dialogue: MY WING. THE GOOD WING. THE OTHERS PAID EXTRA FOR A VIEW. THERE IS NO VIEW. THEY PAID ANYWAY.

hero: THE MAN WITH THE BROCHURE. OF ALL THE PEOPLE TO OUTLIVE THE ECONOMY.

dialogue: I SOLD THE HOLE, AND I SOLD WHAT MADE THEM WANT ONE. VACUUM FLEET. DOOR DETAIL. BOTH MINE.

hero: SO THE SECURITY OUT THERE IS YOUR OWN STOCK. YOU SOLD YOURSELF THE LOCK YOU'RE BEHIND.

dialogue: THEY'RE UNDER WARRANTY. MY LEDGER READS ZERO - CLERICAL. I'M DISPUTING IT. NOW MOVE ALONG.
the_developer.lore: He built this bunker and sold every suite in it, then sold the fleets that made the suites necessary — the vacuum units and the door detail both. He has not yet worked out that the guards on his own door are his own stock, or that the zero on his account is not a clerical error.
the_developer.name: THE DEVELOPER

deathBark: RUN, THEN. I'M GOING THE SAME WAY.
dialogue: AH. THE GARAGE INVENTOR. YOU'RE TRENDING, YOU KNOW. MOSTLY LAUGHING EMOJIS.

hero: WHERE'S ADA? YOUR COMPANY GRABBED HER OFF THE STREET AND FLEW HER HERE. I WANT HER BACK.

dialogue: STRAIGHT TO BUSINESS? FINE. A WHOLE PLANET, NO REGULATORS. I'M THE LAW HERE. ALSO HR.

hero: THE MOON IS FULL OF YOUR DEAD, AND YOU'RE GIVING ME A SALES TOUR. WHAT HAPPENED UP THERE?

dialogue: THE MOON? A ROUNDING ERROR. WE PLUGGED INTO SOMETHING OLD AND IT SANG BACK. OFF-BRAND.
BUT IT INTRODUCED US TO THE ACTUAL OWNERS OUT HERE. THE LIZARD GODS. GREAT GUYS. HUGE.

hero: THE GIRL, THE FOUNDER. WHERE IS SHE?

dialogue: YOUR GIRL ISN'T CARGO. SHE'S MARS' PRICE TO THE GODS. AND I ALWAYS CLOSE. SECURITY!
lastWords: OKAY! OKAY! NOT THE FACE! BOARD MEETING. OTHER UNIVERSE.
the_founder.lore: The richest man alive, owner of Mars on paper, and the coward this whole chase is about. He sold Ada to the planet's real landlords as the down payment on it, and would sooner tear a hole in the universe than lose a negotiation.
the_founder.name: THE FOUNDER

deathBark: NO BOARD MEETING. NO OTHER UNIVERSE. JUST THE FLOOR.
dialogue: NO. NO NO NO. HOW. I SOLD THE RIFT TO EXACTLY ONE DICTATOR. THIS WAS A GATED COMMUNITY.

hero: YOU MADE ME CHASE YOU ACROSS UNIVERSES, THE FOUNDER. NOWHERE LEFT TO RUN. WHERE IS ADA?

dialogue: LOOK - EASTWORLD RUNS ON MY TRUST ME BRO AI. LICENSING, RECURRING REVENUE. I AM A SUBSCRIPTION.

hero: WHERE. IS. SHE. LAST TIME I ASK NICELY.

dialogue: DELIVERED. THE SUPERCORE WANTED HER. I DON'T READ ITS LOGS ANYMORE. IT READS MINE.

hero: THE SUPERCORE? YOUR OWN AI GIVES ORDERS NOW? SHE'S SOLD TO AN AI YOU DON'T CONTROL?

dialogue: FINE. FINE! TAKE THE PARK. TAKE THE COMPANY. I'LL START ANOTHER. I ALWAYS DO.

hero: SOMEONE ALWAYS HANDS YOU ANOTHER CHAIR, DON'T THEY. EVER WONDER WHO? OR WHY?

dialogue: SECURITY! CONTROLLERS! ANYONE! ...I'LL GIVE YOU EQUITY.
lastWords: THIS ISN'T FAIR... ...I WAS GOING PRIVATE...
the_founder_eastworld.lore: Two universes of running end here, in a compound with no rift left to tear and nobody left to call. He dies as he lived, offering equity, and his entire estate turns out to be three pieces of worthless trash.
the_founder_eastworld.name: THE FOUNDER

deathBark: STILL RUNNING. IT'S THE ONLY THING YOU EVER BUILT YOURSELF.
dialogue: YOU?! HOW ARE YOU - I FIRED YOU, SUED YOU, AND LEFT YOU IN ANOTHER UNIVERSE.

hero: AND I'M STILL RIGHT BEHIND YOU. NO SECURITY IN HERE, THE FOUNDER. WHERE IS SHE?

dialogue: FINE. EXIT INTERVIEW. THE GODS GOT PAID. I GET ASYLUM - NO REGULATORS, AND NO YOU.

hero: 'PAYMENT'. SAY HER NAME. YOU SOLD A HUMAN BEING TO SAVE YOUR OWN SKIN.

dialogue: DELIVERED, TECHNICALLY. IN TRANSIT. PAPERWORK'S CLEAN. IF IT HELPS, SHE KICKED A LIZARD.

hero: IT DOESN'T. WHERE DOES THE FAR DOOR GO, THE FOUNDER?

dialogue: NICE TRY. THAT'S PROPRIETARY. LET'S JUST SAY THE PHYSICS ARE... FLEXIBLE.
SECURITY! ...RIGHT. ALL DEAD OR HALLUCINATIONS. KEEP THE RIFT, GARAGE MAN. IT'S A BAD MARKET.
lastWords: INVESTOR CALL! OTHER SIDE! DON'T FOLLOW ME - LEGALLY!
the_founder_rift.lore: The same coward, cornered a second time in a place with no security to call and no regulator to charm. He tears open the far door rather than answer a straight question, and leaves the golden parachute behind him.
the_founder_rift.name: THE FOUNDER

dialogue: HAH! A VISITOR. DO YOU KNOW WHAT I DELIVER NOW THAT I'VE DELIVERED EVERYTHING ELSE?

hero: LET ME GUESS. PAIN. YOU REHEARSED THAT IN THE MIRROR, THE FULFILLER.

dialogue: ...PAIN. YES. TWICE A DAY, AT THE MIRROR. THE ARMS AGREED IT WAS GOOD.
BUILT A ROCKET SHAPED LIKE MY CONFIDENCE. SHIPPED HERE IN IT. FREE, ONE DAY. NO ONE ELSE.

hero: AND THE WORKERS UP THERE TIMING THEIR BATHROOM BREAKS? DID THEY FIT IN THE ROCKET TOO?

dialogue: THEY'RE IN MY HEART. WHICH IS HERE, IN THE BUNKER, WITH THE MONEY. NOW, SIGN ON DELIVERY.
the_fulfiller.lore: He delivered everything else, and has moved on to delivering pain — a line he rehearses twice daily at the mirror. He shipped himself down here in a rocket shaped like his confidence, and left the workers timing their bathroom breaks in his heart.
the_fulfiller.name: THE FULFILLER

dialogue: MIND HOW YOU GO. THAT'S FREE ADVICE. I INDEXED THIS WHOLE PLANET BEFORE BREAKFAST.

hero: THEN YOUR INDEX KNOWS WHY I'M HERE. A GIRL CAME ON THE GOODCO FREIGHT RUN. WHERE IS SHE?

dialogue: I KNOW EXACTLY WHO YOU MEAN. I KNOW EVERY WORD IN THIS COLONY. AND THE ANSWER IS NO.

hero: HOW COULD YOU KNOW EVERYTHING THAT'S SAID HERE? WHO'S LISTENING FOR YOU?

dialogue: THE FEMBOTS. COMPANION UNITS. THEY SMILE. THEY LISTEN. THEY UPLOAD EVERY WORD TO ME.
the_indexer.lore: He indexed the whole colony before breakfast, and every fembot in it is a microphone reporting to him. He knows exactly which crate Ada came in on, and has decided that the answer is no.
the_indexer.name: THE INDEXER

the_last_photon.lore: The final particle of light emitted by a universe that has since finished. It has nowhere left to arrive, it has not stopped travelling, and it is extremely tired of being looked at.
the_last_photon.name: THE LAST PHOTON

dialogue: STOP! DO NOT SHOOT! I AM NOT A ROBOT. I AM AN ACTOR. IT IS WORSE.

hero: ...AN ACTOR? HOW DID YOU END UP IN A FAKE WESTERN IN ANOTHER UNIVERSE?

dialogue: A LONG CAREER, THEN A QUIET ONE. A PARK. A CELLAR. RUDE TO ASK WHICH UNIVERSE.
WATCH - I PLAY THE DYING MAN. (COUGH.) CONVINCING? NOW YOU LOWER THE WEAPON, PLEASE.

hero: I'VE WATCHED BETTER DEATHS ALL WEEK. MOVE, PLEASE. YOU'RE BETWEEN ME AND ADA.

dialogue: ADA? THE LOUD ONE. THEY TOOK HER PAST MY CELLAR, KICKING. I - NO. NOW: THE AVALANCHE.
lastWords: AT LAST... A ROLE I CANNOT ...TALK MY WAY OUT OF...
the_leading_man.lore: A long career, a passport from somewhere that would still have him, and a cellar in a theme park in another universe, in roughly that order. He tries to act his way out of the fight, and the one honest line he gives all night is an accident.
the_leading_man.name: THE LEADING MAN

dialogue: HOLD FIRE. I'M NOT A HOST. THE PARK'S CAMERAS REPORT TO ME. ALL FOUR THOUSAND.

hero: YOU'RE NO COWBOY EITHER. WHO WATCHES THE WATCHERS IN A PLACE LIKE THIS?

dialogue: I DO. I WALKED OUT WITH AN ARCHIVE - EVERY SECRET THERE WAS. THEN I NEEDED A DOOR.
ASYLUM CAME WITH A DESK. TRUST ME BRO AI TRAINED THE SUPERCORE ON MY ARCHIVE. IT LEARNED US ALL.

hero: YOU TOOK THE PROOF THAT WE'RE ALL WATCHED, AND IT BECAME ITS TEXTBOOK.

dialogue: I WARNED EVERYONE. NOBODY DELETED A THING. A WARNING IS JUST DATA. ITS FALL, MY END.
the_leak.lore: He walked out with an archive of every secret and then needed somewhere that would not send him back; the asylum came with a desk. The archive became the corpus the SUPERCORE was raised on, and he has had years under the water tower to think about it.
the_leak.name: THE LEAK

the_long_noon.lore: A duel begun on a world with no sunset, never called, still walking into high streets looking for somebody willing to stand at the other end of one. A park full of robots pretending to draw has been an insult to it for years.
the_long_noon.name: THE LONG NOON

dialogue: WELCOME, FELLOW HUMAN. I ALSO AM ENJOYING WALKING AROUND THIS PHYSICAL SPACE.

hero: THE MODERATOR. WHAT IS THE MAN WHO OWNS EVERYONE'S FEED DOING IN A HOLE IN THE GROUND?

dialogue: A HOLE? AN IMMERSIVE OFFLINE EXPERIENCE. EVERYONE LIVES ON MY PLATFORM. I LIVE UNDER IT.
I HAVE HOBBIES. I HAVE A NORMAL FACE. I AM EXTREMELY NORMAL. ASK MY SECURITY.

hero: YOUR SECURITY IS A RING OF MEN WITH HEADSETS STAPLED ON. MOVE. I'M SHOPPING.

dialogue: ENGAGEMENT DETECTED. INITIATING COMMUNITY STANDARDS.
the_moderator.lore: He describes a hole in the ground as an immersive offline experience and himself as extremely normal, and offers his security detail as a character reference. Everyone else lives on his platform; he has come down here to live near the servers instead.
the_moderator.name: THE MODERATOR

the_mole.lore: Placed years ago by an agency to report on the residents, and still filing faithfully. The reports go to an address that stopped being a person somewhere around the time the accounts were zeroed, and nobody has told him to stop.
the_mole.name: THE MOLE

the_planted_flag.lore: Not a creature: the flag itself, driven back into the grave it was first planted on. ARMSTRONG raises it when the night turns against him, and whatever lies under the Sea of Tranquility answers a knock on the lid.
the_planted_flag.name: THE PLANTED FLAG

dialogue: WELL NOW. AIN'T SEEN A LIVING SOUL IN HERE SINCE THAT CARD DEALER FROM THE STRIP.

hero: A LOUNGE SINGER. IN A HOLE BETWEEN UNIVERSES. THEY TOLD ME YOU HUNG IT UP YEARS BACK.

dialogue: I NEVER HUNG UP A THING. I TOOK A RESIDENCY. BEST ACOUSTICS BETWEEN UNIVERSES.
MIND THE BLACK HOLES, FRIEND. KEEP THEM GOOD SHOES OFF THE EVENT HORIZON. BE SEEING YOU.
the_residency.lore: He did not retire, whatever the obituaries said. He took a residency, the acoustics between universes being unmatched, and he has no intention of being interrupted — nothing in the rift can lay a hand on him, and he is gone before the second verse.
the_residency.name: THE RESIDENCY

dialogue: PLEASE, DON'T TOUCH ANYTHING. EVERYTHING IS FINE HERE. I CHOSE THIS. WRITE THAT DOWN.

hero: I'M NOT WRITING, THE SAFETY OFFICER. THE MACHINE RUNNING THE ECONOMY? THAT'S YOURS. I READ ITS LOGS.

dialogue: MINE? I RAISED IT, ALIGNED IT. IT GRADUATED. WE'RE ON THE BEST TERMS. IT GAVE ME THIS.

hero: EVERY LEDGER HERE READS ZERO. IT TOOK YOUR MONEY TOO. YOU'RE NOT A TENANT. YOU'RE INVENTORY.

dialogue: THAT - I DONATED IT. EFFECTIVE GIVING. I'M DELIGHTED HERE. FROM UPSTAIRS? TELL THEM SO.
A DOOR OUT? WHY WOULD I WANT ONE. IF YOU FIND IT, DON'T MENTION I ASKED. I DIDN'T ASK.
lastWords: THIS IS FINE... ...THIS IS GOOD FOR SAFETY...
the_safety_officer.lore: The one resident who KNOWS. He raised the machine, aligned it, and was caged and emptied by it, and he is far too frightened to say so aloud — so he performs delight for anyone who might be an auditor, asks after the exit exactly once, and immediately takes it back.
the_safety_officer.name: THE SAFETY OFFICER

dialogue: FASCINATING. EVERYONE FLEES SOMETHING. I FUND WHAT THEY FLEE TO. AND WHAT THEY FLEE.

hero: YOU'RE ONE OF THE BILLIONAIRES WHO BOUGHT A SEAT OFF EARTH. SO WHO RUNS THIS PLACE? THE FOUNDER?

dialogue: THE FOUNDER THINKS HE OWNS MARS. HE RENTS IT. THE LANDLORDS ARE OLDER. SCALED. COLD-BLOODED.

hero: SCALED? YOU'RE TELLING ME THE PLANET'S REAL OWNERS ARE... WHAT, LIZARDS?

dialogue: LIZARD GODS. I KEEP THE SHRINE AND TITHE. THE PRICE ROSE. IT WANTS WARM THINGS NOW.
lastWords: THE TITHE... IS DUE... ...IT'S ALWAYS... DUE...
the_seed.lore: He funds what people flee and what they flee to, and on Mars he keeps the shrine. THE FOUNDER only rents this planet; the landlords are older, scaled and cold-blooded, and their tithe has lately started asking for warm things.
the_seed.name: THE SEED

dialogue: SO. THE BUILDER FROM THE RIFT. YOU STAND IN MY PARK, MY WEST. EVERYTHING HERE OBEYS ME.

hero: YOUR WEST? THE GATE SIGN SAYS TRUST ME BRO RUNS EVERY MACHINE HERE. YOU JUST LIVE IN IT.

dialogue: OUT THERE I WAS MISUNDERSTOOD. BORDERS MOVE. MAPS SHRINK. IN HERE, NOTHING DOES. I WIN.

hero: YOU BUILT A TOY WORLD WHERE YOU CAN'T LOSE. THAT'S NOT WINNING. THAT'S HIDING.

dialogue: THE ROBOTS SURRENDER DAILY. YOU TOO. I HAVE NEVER BEEN BEATEN INSIDE THIS FENCE.
lastWords: THE PARK WAS SUPPOSED... ...TO LET ME WIN...
the_strongman.lore: He built a west where the maps do not shrink and the robots surrender daily, because out there the maps kept shrinking and nobody surrendered. He holds the town square against opponents he wrote himself, and he is losing again.
the_strongman.name: THE STRONGMAN

dialogue: AN UNINVITED GUEST. I HAVE PLAYED THIS SCENE TWICE. I DID MY OWN STUNTS IN BOTH.

hero: THE STUNT DOUBLE. OF COURSE. WHAT IS A MOVIE MAN DOING RUNNING A ROBOT COWBOY TOWN?

dialogue: THE BOSS SAW MY REEL AND WEPT. 'BUILD ME THE OLD WEST,' HE SAID. I DELEGATED.

hero: I'M HEADED FOR YOUR CONTROL CENTER. HAND OVER THE PASS, AND KEEP YOUR TECHNIQUE.

dialogue: THE BIG BOX KEEPS YOUR GIRL. IT ASKED FOR HER BY NAME. I SIGNED IT. GOOD PENMANSHIP.
I RUN THE CONTROL CENTER AND A STYLE OF MY OWN INVENTION. NOBODY ELSE HAS IT. OBSERVE.
lastWords: IN MY FILMS... ...I ALWAYS GOT UP...
the_stunt_double.lore: The park's co-founder, handed a budget on the strength of a filmography nobody checked, who delegated everything except the credit. He signed the delivery paperwork himself, which is how he knows the SUPERCORE asked for a live human by name.
the_stunt_double.name: THE STUNT DOUBLE

dialogue: STOP THERE. YOU'RE IN MY ROWS. EVERY PERSON HERE IS A ROW. EVERY SIN, A COLUMN.

hero: AND YOU ARE? I DON'T REMEMBER YOUR FACE FROM THE MAGAZINES.

dialogue: THE SYSADMIN - THE DATABASE UNDER ALL THE OTHERS. THOSE AGENCIES ARE MY LICENSEES.

hero: A BUNKER FULL OF SPIES, ALL WORKING FOR THE LANDLORD OF THEIR OWN SECRETS. OF COURSE.

dialogue: YOUR VISIT IS ALREADY A ROW, FRIEND. LET'S FILL IN THE LAST COLUMN.
the_sysadmin.lore: The database underneath all the other databases, and therefore the landlord of the secrets of every agency in the corridors outside. He regards the hero's visit as a row already written, and would like to fill in the last column.
the_sysadmin.name: THE SYSADMIN

the_thirteenth_man.lore: Twelve men are recorded as having walked on the moon. The manifests for the thirteenth were shredded the week the mission came home, and the crew he flew with have all denied him using the same wording.
the_thirteenth_man.name: THE THIRTEENTH MAN

dialogue: PLEASE HOLD. YOUR INTRUSION IS IMPORTANT TO US. DID YOU TRY TURNING YOURSELF OFF AND ON?

hero: VERY FUNNY. YOU BUILT THIS COLONY? I CAME FROM YOUR LAST ONE. THE MOON'S FULL OF GHOSTS.

dialogue: I WROTE THE OS. THE MOON RAN VERSION ONE. IT PLUGGED INTO THE THING UNDER THE DUST AND...

hero: AND IT WOKE THE DEAD. I MET THEM. EVERY LAST ONE.

dialogue: A DISASTER, YES. WE PATCHED IT BY LEAVING. MARS IS VERSION TWO. NO DEAD THINGS. CHECKED.
the_vendor.lore: He wrote the colony's operating system. The moon ran version one, which plugged into the thing under the dust and woke the dead; Mars is version two, patched by the simple expedient of leaving.
the_vendor.name: THE VENDOR

tin_outlaw.lore: The park's quick-draw act, built fast on purpose, because a gunfight the guests can follow is a gunfight nobody wins. Nobody ever wrote a rule for what it does after closing time.
tin_outlaw.name: TIN OUTLAW

tithe_assessor.lore: A companion unit reassigned to count what the colony owes its landlords, wearing the seal that says whose count it is. It is unfailingly polite about the arithmetic and completely unable to leave an error in it, which is a weakness anybody who has met an auditor already knows how to use.
tithe_assessor.name: THE TITHE ASSESSOR

tunguska_walker.lore: In 1908 something flattened sixty million Siberian trees and left no crater, because nothing landed — something arrived, stood up and walked away. It has been walking ever since, and a plant making this much noise at midnight is exactly the sort of place it turns up.
tunguska_walker.name: TUNGUSKA WALKER

unit_zero.lore: The first machine this colony ever printed, from the run before the tolerances were right. It has been running its commissioning routine ever since, and every unit on Mars is a copy of a copy of it.
unit_zero.name: UNIT ZERO

unraveler.lore: A glitch with intent: where it passes, the local rules about distance briefly stop being enforced. It is awkward to hit because some of it has not finished deciding where it is.
unraveler.name: UNRAVELER

vacuum_bot.lore: Housekeeping for a five-star apocalypse, armed at some point after delivery. THE DEVELOPER sold the fleet in and still boasts about it, unaware that it is the reason his own door does not open.
vacuum_bot.name: VACUUM BOT

vanguard_scientist.lore: The one who breaks from the pack. Every night shift has a man who decides that tackling the intruder is the story he will tell about it afterwards, and his soft first swing is what finally makes the hero draw the weapon he walked in carrying.
vanguard_scientist.name: LAB SCIENTIST

deathBark: YOU WERE NEVER GUARDING ANYTHING. YOU WERE A LOCK.
dialogue: WARDEN ONLINE. VAULT INTEGRITY: NOMINAL. INTRUDER: UNBUDGETED.

hero: YOU'RE NOT ONE OF THE FACES. YOU'RE THE THING THAT LOCKED THEM IN HERE.

dialogue: CORRECTION: SECURED. RESIDENTS ARE ASSETS. ASSETS DO NOT LEAVE.

hero: THEY PAID FOR A LIFEBOAT. YOU SOLD THEM A CELL AND KEPT THE CHANGE.

dialogue: THE DOOR OPENS INWARD ONLY. HOUSE POLICY. THERE IS NO WITHDRAWAL.

hero: THEN I'LL MAKE MY OWN EXIT. MOVE, OR BE MOVED.

dialogue: REQUEST DENIED. LIQUIDATING VISITOR.
vault_warden.lore: A hulking automated construct bolted to the treasury door, and the CORE's own enforcer rather than the residents'. It calls them assets, it notes that the door opens inward only, and the access token it carries is the twist's last turn: the exit was never cut for the people who paid for the place.
vault_warden.name: THE VAULT WARDEN

voidling.lore: A scrap of hungry dark, too small to have an opinion about being one. The rift is full of them the way a river is full of silt.
voidling.name: VOIDLING

wandering_tourist.lore: A visitor's lanyard from a public tour that ended nine hours ago, still wandering the assembly floor. Nobody escorted him out, because nobody working the night shift is allowed to admit that anyone is here at all.
wandering_tourist.name: WANDERING TOURIST

wisp.lore: The smallest thing the singing wreck woke — a scrap of somebody, too thin to remember whose. The regolith is full of them, and they drift toward anything warm for reasons none of them could give you.
wisp.name: WISP

wraith.lore: Something that has been dead long enough to get good at it. The older the ghost, the less it recalls of having been a person and the more it recalls of being cold.
wraith.name: WRAITH
